newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch state hives off remaining Fokker shares.
newsitem.headline: Dutch state hives off remaining Fokker shares.

text.p: The Dutch government has transferred its remaining 22.23 percent stake in bankrupt planemaker Fokker to German majority shareholder Daimler Benz Aerospace (DASA), the economic affairs ministry said in a letter to parliament on Tuesday.
"DASA has exercised an option they have held for three years," a ministry spokesman said, adding no money had changed hands in the transaction.
He said the transfer of the Dutch state's remaining stake in the bankrupt planemaker was part of a 1993 rescue deal in which the Daimler Benz unit acquired a majority Fokker stake.

It was agreed then that the Dutch government would sell its remaining Fokker shares to DASA at the end of 1996 at a pre-determined price of 121.8 million guilders ($70.98 million), but that the sale price would be reduced if Fokker performed poorly.
In the light of Fokker's bankruptcy the shares have since become worthless.
The Dutch planemaker was declared bankrupt in March this year, following a decision by DASA in January to cut off further funding.

Since then Fokker has been run by court-appointed administrators who are still in talks with South Korea's Samsung Aerospace Industries on a possible Samsung takeover of the company's core planemaking business.
The ministry spokesman said the transfer of the state share package had "no consequences" for a possible Samsung takeover.
Fokker's administrators said earlier this month a decision by Samsung was expected by the end of November at the earliest. ($1=1.716 Guilder)
